prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Create ONE standalone track-segment level-design concept image, part of a coherent six-image Bubbleport course design series, inspired by the modular running, obstacle and seated sliding sections of our teddy-bear slide game.
INPUT IMAGE: art-direction reference ONLY. Translate its physical miniature theme-park craftsmanship, ivory resin deck, mint and peach molded plastic, tiny brass connectors, warm inset lamps and translucent mint acrylic. DO NOT copy its entire layout, room, table, buildings, shops, ferris wheel or scenery.
CRITICAL CAMERA: TRUE TOP-DOWN ORTHOGRAPHIC PLAN VIEW, camera exactly vertically above, looking straight down. Image edges parallel to the track edges. Not isometric, not oblique, not a three-quarter render. Objects have realistic 3D material detail and short contact shadows, but only top faces and very small bevels are visible. A clean warm ivory studio background, not a wood table. One track segment only, not a collage, not a full level. Portrait composition for straight segments, generous but small margins, course fills image.
COMMON DESIGN: a wide continuous trough-like racecourse with ivory floor and low mint rails with peach corner caps, similar to our teddy-bear slide tracks. One common lane width of 19.2 design units, a reference character diameter of 1.3 units. Tiny warm signal lenses integrated in rails; no exterior buildings, plants, furniture or crowd. There is visible empty preparation space before every first obstacle and visible empty recovery space after the last. Both ends open for connection, never put an arch across the entry or exit. Simple painted arrowheads indicate travel from bottom to top. Preserve genuinely playable-looking connected floor and clearance; do not place decorations across the route. All motion information is diagrammatic, not additional solid obstacles.
GRAPHIC LANGUAGE: small clean title in top margin only, no paragraphs, no UI, no dimensions. Thin subtle dashed coral sweep envelopes and small bidirectional arrowheads may explain moving hazards, thin dashed teal line with arrowheads may explain ONE suggested player route. Keep these overlays sparse and readable, never obscure the floor. Soft near-photoreal miniature materials with controlled highlights and good contrast, crisp enough for a designer to study the exact obstacle positions.
No text except the specified title and optional small IN/OUT labels. No watermark. No teddy or marble characters. No extraneous obstacle types. Avoid giant blank margins and shallow-depth-of-field blur.
SPECIFIED TITLE: 05 土星回旋滑梯
SEGMENT DESIGN:
One broad180-DEGREE U-TURN DESCENDING SLIDE, not a full circular loop and not a spiral stacked over itself. BOTH open tails at BOTTOM of image, semicircle at TOP. ENTRY lower-left tail travels UP into the left side, turns CLOCKWISE around the TOP of the semicircle and comes DOWN to the lower-right EXIT tail. Floor width19.2, center radius24, straight tails16, height falls8 around the arc. Inner radius14.4, outer33.6; keep thick continuous road, broad clear curvature and smooth tangent joins. Ivory riding floor with mint translucent slide walls and peach rims, use sparse arrowheads following the entire U. Entry tail has a short flat setup zone, exit tail has a visibly longer mint-marked straight braking zone. The courtyard inside U is empty except for a small inset Saturn-shaped PAINT emblem, not a tower, not an obstacle. NO moving hazards in the arc: the route itself teaches sliding and turning; inner dashed peach line is shorter and outer dashed mint line is safer. No connecting floor bridging the space between the two tails; no bridge to a dead-end center island. Exactly one continuous U-shaped trough. Strict overhead orthographic even though this is a descending segment.

corrections.prompt: Precise correction of this existing top-down Bubbleport U-turn slide concept. Preserve the exact U shape, camera, title, material, colors, width and all rails and lights. Travel direction is UP the LEFT tail, CLOCKWISE around the top semicircle, DOWN the RIGHT tail. Make these ONLY changes: 1) Rotate the THREE large white chevron arrowheads inside the green brake strip on the RIGHT EXIT TAIL by180 degrees so they point DOWN toward OUT, matching the teal dashed down arrow above them. 2) The peach inner dashed arc is a shorter player route, NOT moving machinery. Remove its double-headed arrow marks and its backwards-pointing small arrowheads; it should simply be a clean thin peach dashed arc without arrows. Keep the teal outer route arrows, which already correctly run clockwise. 3) Remove the thin raised transverse rim across the bottom of BOTH left IN and right OUT tails. Both full-width floor ends must be OPEN for module connection, flat flush edge with no end wall. Keep the parallel side rails and side corner caps intact. No redesign, no new obstacles, no extra labels.

Make exactly ONE localized correction to this image. In the upper-right quadrant of the U-shaped track curve (approximately the2 o'clock position on the curved road), there is a pair of peach painted chevrons currently pointing UP-LEFT, against the correct traffic flow. Rotate ONLY those two peach chevrons180 degrees in place so they point DOWN-RIGHT, following the clockwise teal dashed route from top of the arc down the right tail. Keep their color, size and location exactly the same. Leave every other arrow, the three white DOWNWARD exit chevrons, text, rails, paths, materials, title and all other pixels unchanged. No redesign. Traffic is UP left tail, across TOP left-to-right, DOWN right tail.
